continuousIntegrals.piece: On each constant-hazard segment [A,A+w], survival S exp(-mu u); integrate exp(-rA)S exp(-(mu+r)u) exactly. Stable exprel/Taylor evaluation for moments0,1,2 avoids cancellation near mu+r=0.
continuousIntegrals.tail: Above100 use sourceL100/l100 as the selected exponential mean; tail hazard is its reciprocal. Infinite stable tail requires mu_tail+r>0. Tail0=S100 exp(-100r)/(mu_tail+r), tail1=tail0*(100+1/(mu_tail+r)), tail2=tail0*(10000+200/(mu_tail+r)+2/(mu_tail+r)^2).
continuousIntegrals.stationary: b=d=1/integral l; mean living age=integral a*l/integral l=E[T^2]/(2E[T]), while mean age at stationary death=e0. Compute positive death integrals separately from b-r.
continuousIntegrals.approximation: For T=mean net maternity age, r>=log(R0)/T by the elementary exponential tangent inequality. Strict if R0!=1 and kernel has positive age variance. The second-order correction is sigma^2*r1^2/(2T); no universal accuracy guarantee.

finiteLaw.state: Annual birth-pulse cohort vector ages0,...,99 plus a100+geometric tail bucket. Survival s_i=l(i+1)/l(i), last-tail survival exp(-mu_tail).
finiteLaw.fertility: K_j=integral_[j-1,j] l(a)m(a)da, j1..55. Top-rowF_i=K_(i+1)/l(i), i0..54. Then B(t)=sum_j K_j B(t-j). This is a declared pulse-census discretization, not the continuous transport semigroup.
finiteLaw.intrinsic: 1=sum K_j lambda^(-j), r_discrete=log(lambda). Analytic stable vector n_i=l(i)lambda^(-i), i0..99, with100+tail l100 lambda^(-100)/(1-exp(-mu_tail)/lambda). Normalize the full101-component vector; compare finite projections only to this same-law target.
finiteLaw.numerical: Normalize for age shares; preserve total-scale logs separately if needed. Initial nonzero sterile older vectors can die out before reproducing and have no target amplitude. Validate zero input/zero fertility/zero future reproductive value explicitly.

renewal.kernel: K(a)=R*a^(k-1)*exp(-a/theta)/(theta^k Gamma(k)); k integer3..8, mean generationT=k*theta.
renewal.forcing: G(t)=B0exp(-t/theta). Positive Neumann convolution series gives B(t)=B0exp(-t/theta)*sum_n R^n(t/theta)^(kn)/(kn)!.
renewal.scaled: c=R^(1/k), z=c*t/theta, dominant r=(c-1)/theta. CorrectedB/B0=exp(-z)*sum_n z^(kn)/(kn)! ->1/k. The roots are(c*omega_j-1)/theta; all other roots have smaller real part.
renewal.reference: Use high-precision positive series; production can use log-sum-exp positive terms or root filtering with an explicit numerical budget. Do not infer positivity from a cancellation-damaged sum. This is an authored renewal-kernel example, not a fitted human maternity schedule.

variableGrowth.example: Own birth history B(t)=exp(r0*t+A*sin(2pi*t/P)), fixed survival l(a)=exp(-mu*a), mu=1/40 and mu+r0>0. n(a,t)=B(t-a)l(a).
variableGrowth.finiteCensus: g_Delta(a,t)=r0+A*(sin(omega*(t+Delta-a))-sin(omega*(t-a)))/Delta. It is a time average, generally not r(a,t).
variableGrowth.normalization: Periodic part integrates over one full period and repeats geometrically with factor exp(-(mu+r0)P). Independent high-precision quadrature versus production Gaussian quadrature; include exact remaining tail beyond the displayed age range. An amplitude0 branch reduces to the exact exponential case.

weakErgodicity.ownProof: For unnormalized x,y>0 define l=min_j x_j/y_j and u=max. Every row of a blockP with m<=P_ij<=M contains at least epsilon=m/M of the common y_j/sum(y) averaging law. Therefore the new ratio range is at most(1-epsilon)(u-l), and its endpoints remain within[l,u]. After one positive block even arbitrary nonzero nonnegative starts are positive. A positive lower ratio persists; total variation tends to0.
weakErgodicity.drawing: Plot actualTV separately from ratio-spread contraction. The TV bound can be very loose; never silently substitute a tighter empirical bound. Plot normalized ratio range against its proved geometric upper bound on a common0..1scale.
weakErgodicity.toy: Four10-year age classes0–9,10–19,20–29,30–39 with exit40; two chosen Leslie laws, reproductive columns2/3 and positive subdiagonals, share a primitive lower-bound pattern. No calibrated human mortality/longevity claim. Pick an actual finite block and prove its minimum positive entry with exactFraction.

twoSex.law: Same explicit4-age toy with separate sex survival/fertility rows. F,G are unconstrained total-birth capacities. Chosen utilization eta<=1/2 and closure B=2etaFG/(F+G),0if either capacity0. This remains at most min(F,G), is homogeneous, and agrees with the alternative etaF/etaG closures at F=G.
twoSex.units: The half-harmonic closure is a chosen birth-production law, not a literal number of exclusive couples. State this directly. Allocate qBfemale and(1-q)Bmale; all controls integer percentages.
twoSex.comparison: Female-only and male-only linear intrinsic rates belong to their separate closures. The two-sex curve shows finite-step growth, not a certified universal nonlinear intrinsic root. Initial absent-sex and eventual-zero totals have explicit undefined-ratio states.
